searchText: <thegaram33> sure, do you have any changes/additions in mind? as Vitalik said L2 state proofs vary, so something like l1staticcall would be more suitable for these. and asking the sequencer to fetch state proofs from any (arbitrary?) L2s might be too much to build into the protocol (re @eliastzr: I wonder if we can build this RIP to cater the needs of the people who most need it; it seems keystore rollups and ens v2 are the most direct candidates? are there other protocols or dapps that need this?) <eliastzr> what l1 contract do you need to call from your l2 in order to need l1staticcall? (re @thegaram33: sure, do you have any changes/additions in mind? as Vitalik said L2 state proofs vary, so something like l1staticcall would be more suitable for these. and asking the sequencer to fetch state proofs from any (arbitrary?) L2s might be too much to build into the protocol) <thegaram33> since each rollup might have a different state proof, they could each deploy a verifier contract on L1 and yo'd call that from L2 using l1staticcall. this is the most generic approach. or, building on l1sload, you can deploy the rollup-x verifier on your L2, and ask someone (e.g. the user) to submit a proof from rollup-x <eliastzr> as rollup sequencer, how do you prove you called the l1 contract with integrity? <thegaram33> create a validity proof of L1 EVM execution (that's why l1staticcall is much more complex than l1sload, at least for zkRollups 😅) (re @eliastzr: as rollup sequencer, how do you prove you called the l1 contract with integrity?) <RenoRen79> Using a groth proof, and the pairing precompile which shall exist, you could design a circuit proving the assessment: "i called this contract, and executed it correctly". (you were faster) <eliastzr> could just run the compute statelessly in a ZK-EVM and verify a STARK? Given these inputs, the EVM execution was correct and here is the output? <RenoRen79> Yes you could. The thing is stark is not standardized on L1, (but definitely should), while you have pairings to run Groth. <vb271828> > are you assuming that a specific L2 core contract exposes an endpoint on L1 to verify inclusion in its tree? Right. That is EIP-3668, it's something that I am trying to push to become a standard among L2s (re @eliastzr: are you assuming that a specific L2 core contract exposes an endpoint on L1 to verify inclusion in its tree? Is that why someone would need to use L1STATICCALL?) <eliastzr> Should it be an entrypoint in the L2’s core contract? (re @vb271828: > are you assuming that a specific L2 core contract exposes an endpoint on L1 to verify inclusion in its tree? Right. That is EIP-3668, it's something that I am trying to push to become a standard among L2s) <vb271828> yeah erc3668 already specifies the name and params of a view function <vb271828> so you would just have the L2 core contract implement that function <eliastzr> I’ll push for Starknet to implement it <vb271828> One of the other idea that we're in the process of figuring out, btw, is moving the de-facto "config" of an L2 to _all_ being callable functions in the L2's core contract on L1 <vb271828> So the only thing you need to know to interact with an L2 (except for RPC URLs) can just be the address <vb271828> similar to how ERC20 works in that sense
